name: Tales of the Rupee
description:
This talk traces the rupee’s five-hundred-year journey across India and beyond, from 1538 to its modern, digital forms. Drawing on a landmark exhibition and the accompanying publication, Odyssey of the Rupee: From India to the World, the session explores how a single denomination carries within it entire histories of economics, commerce, empire, and identity. What can a coin, passed from hand to hand across centuries, still tell us about where we come from? 
Bringing perspectives of numismatists, economists, and historians from the book, the talk examines coinage as more than just currency, but rather as evidence; a material record of the political and economic forces that have shaped our reality. Marking the Republic of India’s rupee at seventy-five years, the session situates this anniversary within a far longer arc, inviting the audience to see the coin in their pocket as the latest chapter in a story centuries in the making.

name: Krishna to Kaveri | ಕೃಷ್ಣೆಯಿಂದ ಕಾವೇರಿವರೆಗೆ
description:
Winding and binding, Karnataka’s great rivers have always been more than glorious waterways. From Krishna to Kaveri, our rivers are carriers of culture, stories, and transformation. As they flow across varied landscapes, they shape and are shaped by the people, traditions, and communities they touch.
Krishna to Kaveri is a two-day celebration that draws from this natural rhythm, exploring how Karnataka’s cultural life is constantly moving, adapting, and renewing itself. From classical roots to contemporary reinterpretations, this festival offers a vibrant weekend that speaks to a new generation. Expect immersive workshops, indulgent cuisines and impactful performances!
Whether you’re a native Kannadiga or recently moved into Bangalore, this festival is for anyone who wants to connect more deeply with the cultural spirit of the region. Not as outsiders looking in, but as participants in a living, flowing cultural journey.
Let the rivers lead. Let culture move. Let Karnataka unfold.
ಬಳಸುತ್ತಾ ಬೆಸೆಯುತ್ತಾ ಬೆಳೆಸುತ್ತಾ ಸಾಗುವ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ನದಿಗಳು ವೈಭವದ ಜಲಹರಿವುಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರವಲ್ಲ. ಕೃಷ್ಣೆಯಿಂದ ಕಾವೇರಿವರೆಗೆ ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸಿರುವ ನದಿಗಳು ಸಂಸ್ಖೃತಿಯ, ಕಥೆ-ಪುರಾಣಗಳ, ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆಯ ಚಲನಶೀಲ ವಾಹಕಗಳಾಗಿವೆ. ವೈವಿಧ್ಯಮಯ ಸುಂದರ ಭೂಪ್ರದೇಶಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಮುನ್ನಡೆವ ಈ ನದಿಗಳು ಜನರನ್ನು, ಪರಂಪರೆಗಳನ್ನು, ಸಮುದಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತಾ, ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಾಗಿ ರೂಪುಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾ ಸಾಗಿವೆ.
ಈ ಸ್ವಾಭಾವಿಕ ಹರಿವಿನ ಲಯದಿಂದ ಹೊಮ್ಮಿರುವ ಎರಡು ದಿನಗಳ ಉತ್ಸವವೆ ‘ಕೃಷ್ಣೆಯಿಂದ ಕಾವೇರಿವರೆಗೆ ʼ. ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಸಾಂಸ್ಕೃತಿಕ ಬದುಕಿನ ನಿರಂತರ ಚಲನೆಯ, ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆಯ, ಪುನಶ್ಚೇತನದ ಶೋಧನೆ. ಈ ಉತ್ಸವವು ಅಭಿಜಾತ ಬೇರುಗಳಿಂದ ವರ್ತಮಾನದ ಮರುವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನಗಳವರೆಗೆ ಹುರುಪಿನ ವಾರಾಂತ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೊಸಪೀಳಿಗೆಗೆ ಒಳನೋಟಗಳನ್ನು ಒದಗಿಸಲಿದೆ. ತಲ್ಲೀನಗೊಳಿಸುವ ಕಾರ್ಯಾಗಾರಗಳು, ರುಚಿಕರ ಆಹಾರ, ಆಕರ್ಷಕ ಸಾಂಸ್ಕೃತಿಕ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮಗಳನ್ನು ಈ ಹಬ್ಬದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಬಹುದು.
ನೀವು ಮೂಲ ಕನ್ನಡಿಗರಾಗಿರಿ ಅಥವಾ ಇತ್ತೀಚೆಗಷ್ಟೆ ಹೊರಗಿನಿಂದ ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿಗೆ ಬಂದಿರುವವರೇ ಆಗಿರಿ. ಈ ನೆಲದ ಸಾಂಸ್ಕೃತಿಕ ಚೇತನದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಆಳವಾಗಿ ಬೆರೆಯುವ ಅವಕಾಶವನ್ನು ಈ ಹಬ್ಬ ನಿಮಗೆ ಒದಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇಲ್ಲಿನ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮಗಳನ್ನು ನೀವು ಹೊರಗಿನವರಾಗಿ ನಿಂತು ನೋಡುವ ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಕರಾಗದೆ ಒಂದು ಜೀವಂತ, ಸಾಂಸ್ಕೃತಿಕ ಯಾನದ ಭಾಗವಾಗಲು ಬನ್ನಿರಿ.
ಮುನ್ನಡೆಸಲಿ ನದಿಗಳು. ಪ್ರವಹಿಸಲಿ ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ. ಗೋಚರವಾಗಲಿ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಸಿರಿ ವೈಭವ!
Schedule coming soon!

Celebrating the Confluences of Karnataka

name: Miracle in Antarctica
description:
70 min | English with English subtitles | 2026 | India 
In December 1983, geophysicist and seismologist Dr. Harsh Kumar Gupta is sent to Antarctica to lead an impossible mission: build Dakshin Gangotri, India’s first scientific base station, before the end of the Antarctic summer. Given a fleeting timeframe of barely sixty days, success would set a world record. Alas, time is not his only adversary. After a blizzard and a helicopter crash, can determination outpace the pack ice? 
The screening of the film will be followed by a discussion with the protagonist and filmmakers. A Q&A with the audience will follow.

name: A Common Ground
description:
Across South Asia, some of the most authentic and quietly radical design is happening at the margins of the profession: in studios working with displaced communities, in student theses that take gender and labour seriously as design questions, and in collectives building in disaster-prone zones. This talk discusses the role of design and architecture in shaping positive social impact across the region. Can architecture and design be practices of collective care rather than individual authorship? 
Practitioners are already proving this to be true. Professionals and students are working with fishermen to rebuild flood-prone coastlines, training self-help groups to construct their own schools, and documenting vernacular knowledge before it disappears. Together, these projects suggest that architecture’s most urgent role today may be relational rather than aesthetic: a tool for redistributing agency over the built environment. 
This event is part of a series of exhibitions, “A Common Ground,” held across Mysuru and Bengaluru, from 26 October to 6 November 2026.

name: We Blog
description:
Write, edit, publish. 
This hands-on workshop brings writers together offline to draft, edit, and self-publish a blog post. Participants work alongside a small community built around in-person blogging, with help at every stage: setting up a blog if you don’t have one, shaping an idea, sharpening the words, and finding the nerve to hit publish. Publicly sharing ideas feels daunting, but anything is possible with a little help from our friends! 
Blogging is hard, and many people spend years searching for a consistent pace. A community can make the process easier, and the end result better. A blog offers a blank slate free of social media algorithms, pairs well with any profession, and lets you link to references. Posts are open to readers without a sign-up barrier, and over time they build into an archive of your own thinking. The only ask is a commitment: write on one topic you care about. 
Please Note: 

Admission is by selection, with limited seats to foster intentional, focused interactions.
Please bring a laptop and a writing idea, so you have something to write on and publish from.

name: Diagnosed and Then?
description:
Written in minutes, a diagnosis is carried for years. But it does not look the same for everyone. 
In honour of World Mental Health Day, themed Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change, this panel brings together people living with mental health conditions and mental health professionals, some of whom are both. It treats experience as knowledge rather than as stories offered for inspiration, and asks what gets lost when a person is reduced to a label. What could be built if knowledge were made together rather than handed down? 
For some, a condition hides behind functioning; for others, it is plainly visible and still not believed, and who gets heard is often decided as much by gender, class, and circumstance as by what is actually happening. Much of what keeps people going happens quietly, in small private repairs that are rarely asked about and too often corrected rather than understood. Panellists deliberate on how to truly co-construct knowledge, care plans, and policies with experts by experience, because you are the only continuous observer of your own life, and that is a kind of expertise.

name: Catch up with Kuchipudi
description:
One morning, many moves! 
This hands-on workshop introduces children to Kuchipudi through the basics of movement and the Natya Shastra, the ancient book of dance on which the form is built. Beginning with a short film about the Kuchipudi village, the session then opens into an exploration of the village and its dance. Learning together with friends, children are invited on a fun and informative adventure into the heritage of Kuchipudi. 
Please Note: 

Seats are limited.
Children should wear comfortable clothes they do not mind getting dirty.

Around the World in 50 Sundays is a journey that begins, not with a ticket, but with opening a book. In a city like Bangalore where families are always in motion, the BIC Library hopes to offer stillness and a quiet, welcoming space for both parents and children where reading becomes a shared experience. Every Sunday, we open our doors to invite you into a library that listens; building a rhythm of return, a habit of joy and a new community bound not just by books, but by the weekly ritual of reading together. 
We welcome your ideas and input. If you have suggestions for children’s events or activities that align with this vision, we’d love to hear from you. Please reach out to us at library@bangaloreinternationalcentre.org
